messages:
emma_cs: FYI customer (acme-inc) hit 403 on both embeddings and generation right after rotating their service key via SCIM. They say it worked before rotation. Error body: {\"code\":\"insufficient_permissions\", \"message\":\"missing inference permission\"}

sam_dev: Can you paste the redacted request and the Authorization header (no secrets) + response body? Also whether they used UI or SCIM to create the key?

emma_cs: Pasting minimal repro with headers (token redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.inference
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{"model":"open-llama-7b", "input":"..."}
```
Response: 403, {\"code\":\"insufficient_permissions\",\"details\":\"missing: inference\"}
Customer says they used Okta SCIM integration to provision the svc account and then rotated keys via their provisioning flow.

devon_platform: I pulled the provisioner run logs for the acme tenant around the rotation time. I see the incoming SCIM \"scopes\" attribute for the svc account was: \"embeddings  rerank \" (two spaces between, trailing space). Our CSV normalizer currently splits on commas only. That results in the final JWT 'scopes' claim being normalized to [\"embeddings\", \"rerank\"] (no inference).

maria_sre: That explains the missing permission. The customer expected scopes to be space-separated; many SCIM clients do that. Our provisioning docs mention comma-separated, but the SCIM connector in Okta exported a space-delimited string. Evidence: provisioner log excerpt:
```
INFO Provisioner: received scopes attribute for acct=svc-acme-rot: 'embeddings  rerank '
DEBUG ScopeParser: split by comma -> [\"embeddings  rerank \"]
DEBUG JwtBuilder: normalized scopes claim -> 'embeddings rerank'
```

auth-bot: Provisioner run 2026-02-25T03:02:14Z: normalized scopes for svc-acme-rot -> [embeddings, rerank]

sam_dev: Thanks. Repro steps for engineers: 1) Create SCIM account with scopes field set to \"embeddings  inference\" (two spaces) 2) Run provisioner -> inspect JWT scopes 3) Call /v1/generate -> 403. I can reproduce locally with an Okta-exported payload.

sam_dev: Working on a fix: update ScopeParser to trim and split on any whitespace in addition to commas. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/4521. Patch also adds a migration run to re-normalize existing svc tokens created in last 7 days.

devon_platform: Short-term mitigation: I re-ran the provisioner for the acme tenant with a forced normalizer that treats whitespace as delimiter. New JWT now contains [embeddings, rerank, inference]. I asked the customer to re-test.

emma_cs: Customer confirms after re-run: generation and embeddings endpoints both succeed. They sent: \"thanks — urgent job unblocked\" :tada:

maria_sre: I'll keep the re-run in place and monitor metrics for 24h (error rate, latency). If stable we'll close. Also filing a KB note and adding a line to the SCIM troubleshooting doc about whitespace-delimited scopes from Okta.

sam_dev: Note: the PR includes unit tests for space/comma/semicolon-separated inputs and a small migration job. We'll canary the deploy to provisioner staging tonight.

emma_cs: Marking customer as unblocked. We'll follow up with a postmortem note to the customer outlining root cause + long-term fix. :thumbsup:

maria_sre: Resolved for now; keeping thread open until 2026-02-26 for final confirmation.
